summaryText:
Scott Williams, a guest preacher from Oklahoma City, brought the message "Don't Chase the Bag" at Impact Church. He built on the closing thought of the recent series "My Wounds Won't Win," which was the difference between chasing the blessing and chasing the Blesser. His text was Numbers 22, the story of Balaam, a man who heard from God but was tempted by the offer of money and status. When Balak's first offer was met with a clear no from God, a bigger and shinier offer followed. Pastor Scott noted that Balaam kept asking God again and began negotiating with what God had already said. He called this disobedience dressed up as discernment. Even before Balaam had the reward, the reward already had him.

Pastor Scott walked through Numbers 22:27-34 and shared several facts about donkeys, including their memory, loyalty, and keen sight, to show how faithfully Balaam's donkey tried to protect him. He then gave three signs that we may be chasing the wrong things. First, others see what we do not. Balaam's anger at his donkey showed how we can lash out at the very people and warnings meant to protect us, whether parents, leaders, friends, or family who pray for us. Second, the warning signs keep progressing. Like a car alarm that gets louder, God may speak through conviction first and then through consequences, detours, or hard seasons, and he can use anything to get our attention. Third, we may be fighting the wrong battle. Balaam thought the donkey was the problem when she was actually protecting his life. Pastor Scott reminded us that not everything that opposes our direction is opposing our destiny, and that our wounds may explain our patterns but do not excuse them.

Throughout the message he invited honest self-examination. He named things people hold onto, such as approval, money, relationships, and habits and addictions. He urged listeners to ask why they keep choosing the same patterns, not only why those patterns keep finding them. He also warned against letting culture redefine what God has said.

The service closed with a powerful response time. Everyone was invited to clench their fists to represent what they hold onto, then open their hands and release it to God, the Potter who holds our lives. People were invited to come to the altar to pray and turn back, and those who had never surrendered their life to Jesus were invited to do so. Pastor Scott led a prayer of salvation, and the congregation celebrated those who responded.
mainPoints: Others may see what you do not: warnings and correction from God and from people who love you are often meant to protect you, not to harm you.
The warning signs keep progressing: if we will not listen to God's conviction, he may speak through consequences, so we should turn back at the first warning.
We can end up fighting the wrong battle: not everything opposing our direction is opposing our destiny, so we should release the bag we are chasing and chase the Blesser instead.

versesMentioned.text: For the Spirit God gave us does not make us timid, but gives us power, love and self-discipline.

When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam. And Balaam's anger was kindled, and he struck the donkey with his staff. Then the LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?" And Balaam said to the donkey, "Because you have made a fool of me. I wish I had a sword in my hand, for then I would kill you." And the donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden all your life long to this day? Is it my habit to treat you this way?" And he said, "No." Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, with his drawn sword in his hand. And he bowed down and fell on his face. And the angel of the LORD said to him, "Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to oppose you because your way is perverse before me. The donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside from me, surely just now I would have killed you and let her live." Then Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned, for I did not know that you stood in the road against me. Now therefore, if it is evil in your sight, I will turn back."
And when the ass saw the angel of the LORD, she fell down under Balaam: and Balaam's anger was kindled, and he smote the ass with a staff.

Monday.scripture: Matthew 6:33 (NIV): "But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well."
Monday.focus: Chase the Blesser, not the blessing.
Monday.action: Before checking your phone or email this morning, spend five quiet minutes thanking God for who he is. Then write down one thing you want from God and ask whether you want God himself even more.
Monday.prayer: Lord, help me to seek you first. Draw my heart toward you more than toward anything you can give me. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: Psalm 139:23-24 (NIV): "Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts. See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting."
Tuesday.action: Take ten minutes to write down what you tend to chase or hold onto (for example approval, money, attention, a habit, or a relationship). Ask God to show you what he sees, and be honest with him.
Tuesday.prayer: God, search my heart and show me what has a hold on me. Give me the courage to be honest and the desire to be free. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: Proverbs 12:15 (NIV): "The way of fools seems right to them, but the wise listen to advice."
Wednesday.focus: Listen to the voices God has placed around you.
Wednesday.action: Ask one trusted person (a parent, mentor, friend, or leader) where they see you heading and what they would encourage you to change. Listen without defending yourself.
Wednesday.prayer: Father, give me a humble and teachable heart. Help me hear the people you have placed in my life to protect me. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Proverbs 28:13 (NIV): "Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy."
Thursday.focus: Turn back at the first warning.
Thursday.action: Choose one specific habit, relationship, or decision that you know is leading you the wrong way. Take one clear step to turn back today, such as confessing to a trusted believer, deleting an app, or ending a harmful pattern.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, I do not want to keep negotiating with what you have already said. Give me strength to turn around and walk in your way. Amen.

Friday.scripture: Proverbs 27:6 (NIV): "Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses."
Friday.focus: Recognize who is on your side.
Friday.action: Think of someone who has corrected you, prayed for you, or spoken honestly to you. Send them a short note of thanks, and if you have misjudged someone, ask for forgiveness.
Friday.prayer: God, thank you for the people who love me enough to tell me the truth and pray for me. Help me to see them as a gift and not as a threat. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: Isaiah 64:8 (NIV): "Yet you, LORD, are our Father. We are the clay, you are the potter; we are all the work of your hand."
Saturday.focus: Open your hands and surrender to the Potter.
Saturday.action: Set aside a few minutes for worship. Play a worship song, open your hands as a sign of release, and name aloud to God what you are letting go. Then plan to attend church this weekend and respond to what God is saying.
Saturday.prayer: Father, my life is in your hands. I release what I have been holding onto. Shape me into who you created me to be. Amen.

title: 3 Signs You’re Chasing the Wrong Thing | Don’t Chase The Bag
